text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Operators of discount houses have submitted a proposal to the Central Bank to allow them to take deposits in response to the recent entry of commercial and merchant banks into the discount business.

- Membership of the Vision 2010 committee, working out an economic development plan, has been enlarged to 194 from the original 172 members, to allow for the discussion of science, engineering and technology.
- Oil marketing companies demand that Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) pays its debts to them, after NNPC cancelled credit facilities to the oil companies.

- South Korea's Daewoo Corporation has secured a $48 million order for materials and services to the Nigerian Liquefied Natural Gas project. Sources said the Daewoo order was part of a sub contract awarded by the consortium handling the main design and construction contract.
- Consumers owe the National Electric Power Authority over 12 billion naira.

- Managing director of Nigerian Breweries says the growth of teetotal pentecostal churches, as well as low consumer spending power, have affected the brewing industry. Felix Ohiwerei said Nigerian Breweries has a growing non-alcoholic product range to give it the support it needs.
- NNPC has assured customers of a continued supply of natural gas following a minor break in a gas pipeline.
- Five Nigeria Airways staff have been sacked over a 26 million naira ticket sales fraud.
